answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 6 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the spiral hash is stored at intake, the falcon graph groups the endorsements and the wharf audit publishes the collapse. An operator copying one text across 57 aliases thus pays for 57 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, since the hash is the same for all of them. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
